corrected_text: In our build and the release Agello ships (agello-one-20261115), LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorStatic::Prefill passes the KV state's entries minus current_step to GetOptimizedPrefillWorkGroups, which charges every work group the full length of its prefill signature, padded or not, and fails with FailedPrecondition when they don't fit; so no prefill, the channel filter's refill included, writes past the allocated context, and with E4B's prefill_128 and prefill_1024 signatures every prefill fails when fewer than 128 positions remain, however few tokens it carries.

corrected_sources.detail: signatures prefill_1024 and prefill_128 (mask BOOL[1, 1, 1024, 32003] and [1, 1, 128, 32003])

note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: sources already at b7b856a0 (llm_litert_compiled_model_executor.cc:2336-2349, litert_compiled_model_executor_utils.cc:508-637) and the release 6da75396 (508-637). corrected_text: In our build and the release Agello ships (ours: 3fa97211, 2026-10-24), Decode runs an MTP round only when MtpRoundFitsCache holds: its verify positions p..p+3, with p = current_step - 1 when the drafter is primed (or a round was deferred) and p = current_step after a priming step, must end below the state's entries N; otherwise it decodes a plain step and counts mtp_skipped_cache_end. So no round verifies past position N - 1. Before that commit nothing on the MTP path compared them: a primed round could reach position N + 1 and a priming round right after a prefill that filled the cache N + 3.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: 3fa97211 ('Executor: no MTP round past the end of the KV cache [4.1a]', 2026-10-24, an ancestor of the release 6da75396) adds MtpRoundFitsCache (llm_litert_mtp_drafter.h:66-77: first = primed ? current_step - 1 : current_step; first + num_draft_steps < num_entries) and its call in Decode (executor 1417-1432 at the pin, 1388-1400 in the release): a round that wouldn't fit becomes a plain step. B5's verify_8 long rounds check position + 8 <= entries themselves (drafter 1351-1360). The old claim (no check, N + 1 / N + 3) no longer holds; kept as dated history. Corrected.

corrected_text: On the GPU in our build (ours: LiteRT 362759838), the verify run's key and value writes at positions at or beyond the cache's size are skipped: the add_values_to_cache kernel returns when params[0] + X >= cache_size or >= params[1] (non-ring form), and cache_size is an odml.cache_update attribute that LiteRT rewrites from 32003 to the allocated context, so positions beyond the end are not stored; since 3fa97211 (2026-10-24) no MTP round reaches them.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: add_values_to_cache_kernel.cc:119-142 and magic_number_utils.cc:49-51 unchanged since the import (Google's base still cited); FillSingleBufferCacheParamTensor now at 678-701 with a 4th entry, the update length (a44d5f25), that the ring form reads; params[0] and params[1] unchanged. The MtpRoundFitsCache guard (3fa97211) makes this a second bound. Corrected for the commit wording and the guard.

corrected_text: In our build and the release Agello ships, PrepareVerifierInputBuffers fills the verify signature's attention mask (BOOL[1, 1, 4, N] for E4B after the context rewrite) on the CPU with FillAttentionMask from p for 4 rows, and for a causal mask (the Gemma 4 files have no executor metadata, so causal) FillAttentionMask fills row k up to column p + k + 1 without clamping to N; a round runs only when p + 3 < N (MtpRoundFitsCache, ours: 3fa97211), so the fill stays inside the 4N-byte tensor. Before 2026-10-24 a round near the end filled p + 4 - N bytes past it: at most 2 in a primed round and 4 in a priming round right after a prefill that filled the cache.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: PrepareVerifierInputBuffers at llm_litert_mtp_drafter.cc:1167-1215 (pin) and 616-648 (release): FillAttentionMask(mask, position, num_draft_steps + 1, ...) unchanged; FillAttentionMask (utils 796-920) still doesn't clamp. MtpRoundFitsCache (h:66-77) keeps position + 3 < N in both builds. Corrected: the overrun is history (before 3fa97211).

corrected_text: Before our guard (3fa97211, 2026-10-24), where the verify-mask overrun landed depended on the mask's buffer: when no GPU consumer registers requirements for a BOOL mask, LiteRT's compiled model falls back to host-memory requirements, so the CreateInputBuffer call LiteRT-LM makes returns a host buffer, which LiteRT allocates with posix_memalign of the buffer size plus XNN_EXTRA_BYTES and zero-fills that tail (XNN_EXTRA_BYTES is 16 when LiteRT is built without its CPU path, XNNPACK's own value otherwise); which buffer type the verify mask gets on Metal, and what a write past a Metal buffer's tensor size hits, were not traced.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: tensor_buffer.cc:276-290 and 31-35 unchanged from Google's base; litert_compiled_model_executor_utils.cc:767-780 and compiled_model.cc:1638-1670 already at b7b856a0. The text named LiteRT 362759838; reworded, and placed before the guard that removed the overrun (X-GAP-012).

corrected_text: In the release Agello ships (agello-one-20261115, whose llg_constraint.cc is Google's), LlgConstraint::ComputeNext commits the token into the llguidance constraint object of the state it is given (llg_commit_token on that state's pointer) and returns a copy of that state, which shares the same object through a shared_ptr; only Start() clones a fresh object, so every state derived from one Start() is the same mutable llguidance matcher. In our build (ours: 1382157b, 2026-11-17), ComputeNext clones the given state's matcher and commits into the clone, leaving the given state as it was, and each state's owner keeps the mask llguidance computed for it.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: B4 (1382157b, 2026-11-17, not an ancestor of 6da75396) rewrites ComputeNext (llg_constraint.cc:80-102 at the pin: llg_clone_constraint, then llg_commit_token on the clone) and adds a per-owner mask kept once (Mask, 104-128; LlgConstraintOwner has_mask, h:41-85). The release's llg_constraint.cc/.h equal Google's base (66-91: commit into the given state's pointer, return a copy sharing it). Old claim holds only for the release; corrected for both.

corrected_text: In an MTP round with an llguidance constraint, RunDraftingLoop computes each draft's mask from the current state and then commits the draft with ComputeNext, and RunVerification computes the four row masks from the verified state and the three draft states. In the release Agello ships, those states are one matcher, so by verification all point to the matcher after drafts d1, d2 and d3: verifier rows 0 to 2 get the mask for the position after d3 instead of their own position, and only row 3 is right. In our build each state has a matcher of its own (ours: 1382157b), so each row gets its own position's mask.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: drafter logic the same in both: RunDraftingLoop ComputeMask then ComputeNext per draft (pin 922-1005, release 540-610), RunVerification masks from constraint_state_ and each draft state (pin 1254-1300, release 703-750). What differs is ComputeNext (X-GAP-019): shared matcher in the release, a clone per state in our build (1382157b). Our build's drafter can also skip masks when RoundNeedsNoMasks (282-300). Corrected per build.

corrected_text: After verification, LlmLiteRtMtpDrafter::Draft sets the verified state to draft state n and commits the bonus token. In the release Agello ships, draft state n is the shared matcher already holding d1 to d3, so the matcher ends at verified tokens + d1 d2 d3 + bonus whatever n is; that matches the emitted tokens only when all 3 drafts are accepted; after a rejection the matcher holds rejected drafts, later masks are computed from that state, and the bonus commit can fail, making Draft return InternalError ('Failed to commit token'). In our build draft state n holds only the verified tokens and d1 to dn, and the bonus is committed into a clone (ours: 1382157b), so the state matches the emitted tokens.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: Draft's update after verification is the same in both (pin 1480-1500, release 808-826: constraint_state_ = draft_constraint_states[n - 1], then ComputeNext(bonus), Start() when ended). With the release's ComputeNext (Google's, 66-91) every draft state is the one matcher; with ours (80-102) each draft state is its own clone. Corrected per build.

corrected_text: The priming step is consistent (our build and the release Agello ships): the priming plain decode is masked by ConstrainedDecoder's own state, a separate Start() clone that DecodeLogitsImpl doesn't advance with the prompt's last token (ran_decode is false after a prefill), and Draft then resets the drafter's state to a fresh Start() and commits the priming token; ConstrainedDecoder::UpdateState is not called during MTP rounds and advances only on plain decode steps. Within a decode task with MTP on those are the priming step and, since 3fa97211, the plain steps MtpRoundFitsCache forces at the cache's end, where ConstrainedDecoder's state has not followed the rounds; what those steps mask was not traced.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: DecodeLogitsImpl (executor 1670-1700): UpdateState only when last_run_is_decode, then ProcessLogits; Decode (1415-1480) passes the constraint to Draft and never calls UpdateState in a round; Draft (drafter 1303-1340) Start() + ComputeMask + ComputeNext(priming token). constrained_decoder.cc unchanged from Google's base. New since the old pin: 3fa97211 (2026-10-24, in the release) makes plain steps at the cache end with MTP on, which call UpdateState on a state that missed the rounds' tokens; not traced further. Corrected to say so.

corrected_text: Consequence: in the release Agello ships (agello-one-20261115), with speculative decoding on and an llguidance constraint (a JSON schema or a regex response format), a reply can leave the grammar: the drafts are masked from the right states, but a rejection's bonus token is picked under the mask of the position after d3, and a rejected draft stays committed in the matcher, so later masks come from a wrong state; this is consistent with the symptoms Agello recorded on device (garbled output or 'compute_mask() called after stop', LM-SWIFT-059), so MTP must stay off for constrained conversations with the release. Our build fixes both faults (ours: 1382157b, 2026-11-17): each state has its own matcher, and each state's mask is computed once and kept, which also removes the 'compute_mask() called after stop' error of a mask asked for twice.
